description: Expected results for the official pyswmm test model pyswmm/tests/data/model_storage_pump.inp (pyswmm v2.1.0, git 80b9d55). One subcatchment, junctions J1/J2, pump P1 into storage unit SU1, outfall J3, constant 20 cfs inflow with pollutant 'test', DYNWAVE routing 1 s, 2015-11-01 14:00 to 2015-11-04 00:00. inputs/ is the unmodified file from the pyswmm git tree (git show HEAD:...).

numeric_checks.name: SU1_storage_max_volume
numeric_checks.why: largest volume held in storage unit SU1 (ft3)

numeric_checks.name: SU1_storage_max_vol_date
numeric_checks.why: date of max SU1 volume (days since 1899-12-30); tol = half the official gap only (a % band makes no sense for a date)

numeric_checks.name: SU1_peak_total_inflow
numeric_checks.why: peak inflow into SU1 = pump P1 rate (cfs)

finished_normally: KI tool exit code 0 and JSON status 'completed'; report has 'Analysis begun on' and 'Analysis ended on' and no ERROR; statistics run exit code 0
recorded_with: /mnt/disk1/Hydrocraft_server/python_env/bin/python (pyswmm 2.1.0, swmm-toolkit 0.17.0), KI tools/run_pyswmm.py + a statistics pass that copies pyswmm's own test procedure
reference: Official values come from pyswmm/tests/test_nodes.py (test_storage_7, test_outfalls_8). Where the official test asserts two values (e.g. 4979 and 4980), expected = their middle and tol = half their gap + 0.1%. The official test uses pytest.approx(rel=UT_PRECISION) with UT_PRECISION=1 (meant as 1%, but pytest reads it as 100%), so it is very loose; the tolerance here is much tighter. Own-run values for this run (2026-10-05): SU1 flooding_volume 621394.5, J3 total_periods 208797, J3 pollutant 1756.2078, J3 cumulative_inflow 1876901.2 - each within 0.001% of the nearest official value.
notes: Two clean runs gave identical numbers. The pyswmm getters sim.runoff_error/flow_routing_error read inside the run return 0.0, while the report says -0.002% routing error; the report value is used here.
